title: Vitamin D Test
attribution: Source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine.
measures: Measures vitamin D in the blood, usually as 25-hydroxyvitamin D, to show whether the body has enough. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for healthy bones and teeth and supports muscles, nerves and the immune system.
low: Results may be reported as deficient or insufficient. Possible reasons include not getting enough from diet or sunlight, trouble absorbing it from food, trouble converting it into a usable form (which may point to kidney or liver disease), or a medicine that affects the level.
high: A high or toxic result usually follows taking too much from supplements. Excess vitamin D can seriously damage organs and blood vessels, and may cause nausea, vomiting, poor appetite, constipation, muscle weakness and weight loss.
notes: Total vitamin D, the sum of D2 and D3, is the key number. Routine testing is not recommended for everyone.
